title: Orbit Consortium readiness playbook and acceptance plan
content:
Purpose:
This is the Orbit Consortium readiness playbook for the upcoming evaluation window. The document aligns engineering, solutions, and customer teams on scope, operational guardrails, measurable acceptance criteria, and the workshop agenda for the first two-week onboarding sprint. Use this doc as the single source of truth for go/no-go decisions during the evaluation period.

Context and constraints:
- Customer: Orbit Consortium (multi-tenant knowledge base + UX search use case).
- Goal: Validate Redwood inference integration for semantic search, snippet generation, and reranking against Orbit's internal corpus (~200k docs) with realistic QPS.
- Environment: Dedicated trial cluster in us-west-2 (staging VPC). Private data must never leave customer VPC; all data ingestion via SFTP and KMS-wrapped keys.
- Timebox: 2-week technical evaluation, followed by a 2-week acceptance window for performance regression and cost validation.

Success criteria (quantitative):
- Relevance/quality: Mean NDCG@10 >= 0.68 on Orbit evaluation set (baseline: 0.61).
- Latency: 95th percentile for end-to-end query (request + inference) <= 220ms at 10 QPS sustained.
- Throughput: Sustained 50 QPS burst-capable to 120 QPS for short spikes with <2s tail latency increase.
- Cost: Estimated per-query inference cost <= 0.9x of Redwood internal baseline for comparable model config (after batching).
- Reliability: Error rate <= 0.3% over each 24-hour window; no single outage >5 min.
- Data handling: All ingested documents encrypted at rest with customer KMS key; logs scrubbed of PII before leaving VPC.

Acceptance criteria (technical checklist):
- Model integration: Redwood model and reranker variant deployed, validated with a smoke test set (pass if <2 dropouts out of 200 queries).
- End-to-end pipeline: Ingest->index->query flow exercises KV caching and prefix caching at least once; artifacts uploaded to staging S3.
- Observability: Traces arriving in Console for token-level breakdown, per-route latency heatmaps, and cost by token for the evaluation period.
- Rollout policy: Canary config deployed (5% traffic) with automatic metric rollback on NDCG regression >3% vs. control.
- Security: VPN/Tunnel established, service account permissions scoped, audit logging enabled.
- Ops runbook: Clear escalation path documented (oncall, SE owner, SRE contact).

Workshop agenda (Day 0 to Day 3):
- Pre-work (Day -2): Customer provides sample subset (10k docs), API access to identity service, and KMS key fingerprint. SEs validate SFTP and test ingestion. Owners: Asha (redwood), Orbit infra lead (customer).
- Day 0 (kickoff, 90m): Introductions; success metrics review; confirm data handling and legal constraints; align timeline. Owners: Asha (host), Orbit PM.
- Day 1 (technical deep-dive, 3h): Architecture walkthrough, model selection tradeoffs, batching/latency tuning, and quantization options. Demos: local rerank baseline vs. Redwood model. Owners: Liam (model), Sofia (runtime).
- Day 2 (ingestion & indexing, 4h): Hands-on ingest of 10k sample, index verification, and search smoke tests. Owners: Jordan (ingest), Eileen (indexing).
- Day 3 (observability & acceptance run, 2h): Setup dashboards, run the first evaluation sweep, capture initial metrics. Owners: Asha (measurement).

Roles and responsibilities:
- Redwood SE lead: Asha Menon — program owner, workshop facilitator, acceptance decision authority for infra/model readiness.
- Redwood model lead: Liam Patel — model selection, eval config, and quality measurements.
- Redwood runtime lead: Sofia Martinez — batching, caching, and latency tuning.
- Customer integration lead: Orbit infra lead (name TBD) — dataset access, VPC peering, schema owners.
- SRE contact: Eileen Park — cluster provisioning, SLA monitoring, incident response.

Technical prerequisites (customer action items):
- Provide 3 sample datasets: minimal (1k), test (10k), full (200k) in agreed format (JSONL).
- Confirm KMS details and SFTP creds by Day -2.
- Whitelist Redwood staging egress IPs (list shared in Slack).
- Allocate internal product SME for daily 30-min sync during the trial.

Evaluation methodology:
- Metrics: NDCG@10, MRR, latency p50/p95, token cost per query, error rate.
- Protocol: Run 3 sweeps per day during a 48-hour window at target QPS levels (10/QPS, 50/QPS stress). Capture and snapshot model outputs for human review.
- Human eval: Product SME reviews 100 random queries per sweep; flag regressions or hallucinations.
- Regression gating: Any drop in NDCG@10 > 0.03 triggers rollback and post-mortem.

Risk matrix and mitigations:
- Data leak risk: High for un-scrubbed logs. Mitigation: enforce log-scrubbing lambda and KMS-only exports.
- Latency blowups under burst: Medium. Mitigation: configure autoscale + soft-fallback to lower-cost model variant with degraded but acceptable NDCG.
- Model quality drift: Medium. Mitigation: freeze prompt templates and evaluation harness; rerun baseline daily.
- Permission/configuration delays: Low/Medium. Mitigation: escalation path documented; contingency day added to schedule.

Fallback and graceful degradation plan:
- If 95p latency > 350ms for >10 minutes, route queries to cached responses (prefix cache) and notify customer via Slack channel #se-orbit-onboard.
- If model quality drops below threshold, automatically fallback to reranker-only pipeline while blocking model rollout.

Open questions (action owners):
- Can Orbit provide anonymized human labels for 2k queries to bootstrap NDCG calc? (Owner: Orbit PM)
- Is there a contractual limit on daily network egress from staging VPC? (Owner: Orbit infra)
- Confirm retention window for logs in Redwood Console for trial (Owner: Asha).

Deliverables and timeline (high level):
- Day -2: Pre-work completed (data + creds).
- Day 0-3: Workshop and initial smoke tests.
- Day 4-14: Evaluation sweeps, tuning, and dashboards.
- Day 15-28: Acceptance window; business sign-off and pricing discussion.

Communication cadence and channels:
- Daily 30-minute standup during Day 0-14 (time: 09:30 PT).
- Slack: #se-orbit-onboard (ops/alerts), #se-orbit-discussion (product/quality).
- Confluence page: confluence:SE-ORBIT-READINESS-2025 (link in metadata).

Post-trial decision rubric (what 'pass' means):
- Met all quantitative success criteria for 7 consecutive days in acceptance window.
- No critical security issues discovered in audit.
- Customer product SME signs off on quality (human eval pass rate >= 85% across samples).
- Commercial alignment: preliminary pricing within 15% of projected unit economics.

Appendix: quick runbook snippets
- How to trigger a rollback: Console -> Rollouts -> Select canary -> Rollback -> Confirm. (Owner: SRE)
- Contact list: Asha Menon (asha@redwood.com), Liam Patel (liam@redwood.com), Sofia Martinez (sofia@redwood.com), Jordan Nguyen (jordan@redwood.com), Eileen Park (eileen@redwood.com).
- Useful tickets/links: JIRA:SE-8572 (trial infra), PR: github.com/redwood-inference/orbit-integration/pull/58

Notes to self (informal):
- Bring up a lightweight baseline reranker if ingestion stalls; low-risk demo for product.
- Make sure demo corpus includes some long-tail docs (legal templates) — often breaks reranker.
- Double-check KMS policy transforms for cross-account decrypt.

Next steps (immediate):
- Asha: schedule Day 0 90m kickoff with Orbit PM and legal (by 2025-11-07).
- Liam: prepare baseline eval harness and 10k smoke queries (by Day -1).
- Sofia: preconfigure batching profiles for 10/50/120 QPS and have them ready to toggle.

-- end of playbook --
